comment: Canopy share per committed test area (data, not code), for the profiles' trees.canopyShare. Each area is the area manifest's rectangle (centre, width, height) laid out in the NAIP item's UTM grid; streets and parks come from the committed osm.json (no new Overpass request). NAIP = newest acquisition of the state at the area; when one quarter-quad does not cover the whole area, the newest year's items are mosaicked (first item wins where they overlap). Canopy method and thresholds: data/params.json `canopy` (unchanged from the Wilmette study).
parkComment: Parks are public open space removed for the residential-fabric share. landuse=grass (1,551 small lawn and parkway polygons at Sloan's Lake), meadow and scrub are not parks: they sit inside residential blocks and their street trees belong to the fabric. Park polygons under parkMinAreaM2 are ignored.

areas.crownSource: lidar, Lakeview clear of buildings (13.4; all detected trees 92 m2)
borrowed: mean of the three Illinois lidar areas (no lidar run in Denver)
calibrated effective mask-canopy area per tree (aerial.md 13.10): 14 plots of 50 m, hand count and lidar tops (lidar-roofs.md 13.4: crown 108 m2 before calibration)

calibration.basis: 14 random 50 m plots over the built fabric (stable seed), trees counted by eye on 0.3 m NAIP (189) and as lidar tree tops in the same plots (159); effective crown = mask canopy area / trees, mean of the two counts; interval = bootstrap over plots, range spans both counts
calibration.note: treesPerHa uses the mask canopyShare of each block; the label-corrected share is reported, not applied (the mask over-calls tree shade; the plot ratio is computed on the same mask, so the over-call cancels)

areas.crownSource: area-specific effective mask-canopy area per tree (aerial.md 13.10): 6 plots of 50 m counted by eye, scaled by the Wilmette lidar-mid / eye ratio (1.086); no lidar run at Winnetka

calibration.basis: 6 random 50 m plots, trees counted by eye on 0.3 m NAIP (122); eye-only effective crown 85.6 m2 (bootstrap 80.9-89.9), multiplied by Wilmette 121.3/111.7 so that it is on the same eye-and-lidar basis; range = Wilmette ratios (0.835, 1.18) around the estimate
calibration.note: Wilmette calibration (121 m2) does not transfer: Winnetka eye-only 85.6 m2 lies outside Wilmette 101-123. Dense plots (merged crowns) are counted with an uncertainty of about 25 percent

areas.crownSource: area-specific effective mask-canopy area per tree (aerial.md 13.10): 6 plots of 50 m counted by eye, scaled by the Wilmette lidar-mid / eye ratio (1.086); no lidar run at Kenilworth

calibration.basis: 6 random 50 m plots, trees counted by eye on 0.3 m NAIP (97); eye-only effective crown 99.4 m2 (bootstrap 90.8-110.3), multiplied by Wilmette 121.3/111.7 so that it is on the same eye-and-lidar basis; range = Wilmette ratios (0.835, 1.18) around the estimate
calibration.note: Eye-only interval overlaps Wilmette (101-123); the own-area value is used because six plots cannot separate the two. Dense plots (merged crowns) are counted with an uncertainty of about 25 percent
